sara: Heads up — staging p99 jumped after the 09:00 deploy. We paused the rollout. Notable: model checkpoint bumped + tokenizer config tweak in same release.
perf-ci-bot: ALERT: perf/regression detected in job=staging-inference-ci run=2026-03-18T09:12 id=ci-8792 
  metric: p99_latency_ms 
  baseline: 142.3 -> current: 221.7 (+55.7%) 
  suspect commits: 9a1f3b2, 4c7e2d1 
  link: https://ci.redwood/ci-8792/details
kevin: Which commits exactly? 9a1f3b2 is the model-onboard bump, 4c7e2d1 is the batching heuristic change right? Any kernel-fallback logs in monterey?
oliver: quick grep in the node logs shows a lot of these during the spike:
```
W kernel-router: selected fallback_kernel for model=redwood-xl-3b quant=fp16 seq=512
I kvcache: eviction_count=1294 hot_evictions=387
I batch-scheduler: emitted small-batches=2375 avg_batch_size=1.9
```
Seems we started routing to fallback kernels a lot more.
dinesh: Yep — my PR #3421 adjusted the batch heuristic (min_batch_window from 0.05 -> 0.02s) to reduce tail latency under heavy load. I didn't expect it to increase small batch churn for short prompts. PR: https://git.redwood/pr/3421 commit=4c7e2d1
maya: Also important — tokenizer config change in the model-bump PR turned off the fast tokenizer for this checkpoint (use_fast=false). That increases tokenization variance and slightly changes avg seq lengths (more short sequences padded differently). Could make small-batch ratio worse. Commit=9a1f3b2
kevin: OK that combo is suspicious: smaller batching window + more short requests => more batches, smaller avg batch size => kernel selection falls back to generic slower kernels. Can we reproduce with the staging model locally? Run with a traffic replay of short prompts.
oliver: Ran a synthetic replay on a staging node. Microbench (1000 requests of len~8):
```
baseline (old heur=0.05, fast tokenizer): p99=135ms avg_batch=6.1
current (heur=0.02, no-fast-tokenizer): p99=219ms avg_batch=2.0
forcing optimized kernel (REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=optimized_v2): p99=148ms avg_batch=2.0
```
So kernel selection is the big hit when fallback is picked, batching change amplifies it. Forcing kernel helps but isn't ideal.
sara: Thanks. What's our bisect plan? Best to revert batching heuristic first (fast to change) or revert tokenizer setting? Which is lower risk for rollout?
dinesh: I'll open a hotfix to revert the min_batch_window to 0.05 and add a regression CI test that replays short-prompt workload. If that brings p99 down we can leave tokenizer change in and iterate. Opening PR now: https://git.redwood/pr/3489 commit=7b2c4d8
deploy-bot: ROLLOUT STATUS: rollout paused for release/2026-03-18-09:00 due to perf regression. Blockers: PR/3489 or revert of model-onboard PR.
kevin: Good. Owners: dinesh on batching revert, oliver on perf verify + benchmark artifacts, maya to check whether tokenizer change is necessary for the onboarded checkpoint. If PR/3489 fixes staging p99 we'll proceed with a canary.
sara: Agreed. Please post perf numbers to the ticket and we can unpause once canary passes. Also add metrics for kvcache evictions in the regression test (that hot eviction count looked noisy). :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll also add a short-term mitigation: clamp min_batch_window to 0.03 for dedicated pools that serve many short prompts, and follow up with a smarter adaptive window that accounts for seq length distribution.
oliver: I'll attach the profiler traces to the ticket (flamegraph + kernel-call counts).
sara: Thanks team — leaving this thread for updates.
